title: Not My Idea of a "Tad", "Dash", "Pinch", or "Smidgen"
text:
Not My Idea of a "Tad", "Dash", "Pinch", or "Smidgen". These stainless steel NORPRO MINI MEASURING SPOONS will make a cute joke gift for a serious cook, but they're not really useful as measuring spoons (tad, dash, pinch, smidgen, drop), because the measures are overly generous. If you use them with old recipes that call for these amounts, you'll probably overseason your dishes.

My mother taught me that in old recipes, a "tad" is a small amount; a "dash" is one shake from a shaker (e.g., a pepper or salt shaker); a "pinch" is the amount you can pinch between your finger and thumb; a "smidgen" is a very tiny amount (just enough to achieve the right taste); and a "drop" is one drop of liquid (e.g., a drop from a food coloring bottle). Of course these are only approximations, but they're used primarily to mean "cautiously season to taste".

In this set, a "tad" is a scant 1/4 teaspoon; a "dash" is a scant 1/8 teaspoon; a "pinch" is 1/16 teaspoon; a "smidgen" is 1/32 teaspoon; and a "drop" is a generous single drop of food coloring liquid. To me, 1/4 teaspoon is way more than a "tad", and 1/8 teaspoon is much more than a "dash". My idea of a "pinch" matches up with Norpro's idea of a "smidgen".

In sum, these are NOT the really small measuring spoons that I expected (spoons that would measure amounts of 1/8 teaspoon or less). They are well made, of solid stainless steel, and they are dishwasher safe. However, because they measure overly large amounts, I rate them at 2 stars ("I don't like them" on the official Amazon scale).
